traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and named requirements in docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md are implemented and verified: - The valid-annotation-format rule now supports both nested and flat configuration for story/requirement patterns (`story.pattern`/`req.pattern`, `storyPathPattern`/`requirementIdPattern`) and example strings (`story.example`/`req.example`, `storyPathExample`/`requirementIdExample`). - Regex strings are compiled defensively; invalid patterns yield configuration errors via the invalidRuleConfiguration message while the rule falls back to default patterns, preserving behavior. - When options are omitted, the rule uses the original hardcoded patterns and examples, and existing tests for base behavior continue to pass, satisfying backward compatibility. - Error messages dynamically incorporate configured example strings, with nested examples overriding flat shorthands as specified. - A JSON Schema describes all new options and is hooked into the rule meta schema, aligning with ESLint best practices. - Integration with valid-story-reference is clean and consistent: format validation is separated from existence checks, and both can be configured together. - The story’s own tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts are explicitly tagged for this story and all pass in the most recent `npm test -- --verbose` run. Therefore this story is fully implemented and currently passing all tests.
